title: Big Cats
objective: After this level you can describe lions, tigers and the other big cats.
summary: Panthera cats (lions, tigers, leopards, jaguars) often roar; small cats' hardened hyoid prevents it. Lions live in prides where lionesses hunt; tigers, the largest cats, live alone.

cards.headline: Your house cat will never roar. It isn't shy.
cards.body: A lion's roar can be heard up to five miles away. A house cat can't make that sound at all, however big its attitude. The difference comes down to one small bone.

cards.headline: The roaring club
cards.body: Level 4 put lions, tigers, leopards and jaguars in one genus, Panthera. These are the big cats, and they often roar. Smaller cats have a fully hardened hyoid, a small bone in the neck, and that stiff bone prevents them from roaring. Same family, different hardware.

Except when mating or raising young

cards.headline: A roar is a property line
cards.body: A pride can hold as many as 40 lions, and it has ground to defend. Both males and females roar to mark their territory, and the sound carries up to five miles. The lionesses bring home the dinner; the roar tells every other lion whose ground this is. Think of it as a fence you can hear from the next town.

questions.prompt: Lions, tigers, leopards and jaguars share Level 4's genus Panthera. What stops smaller cats from roaring?

options.label: Their lungs are too small
options.rationale: The cause is a bone, not the lungs.

options.label: They have no vocal cords
options.rationale: Small cats meow, so they have vocal cords.

questions.explanation: Smaller cats have a fully hardened (ossified) hyoid bone that prevents roaring.

questions.prompt: Lions and tigers are both big cats. What is the biggest difference in how they live?

options.label: Lions live in prides; tigers live alone
Tigers live in prides; lions live alone

questions.explanation: Lions are the most social cats, living in prides; tigers are solitary except when mating or raising young.

questions.prompt: Level 6 said every cat must eat meat. In a lion pride, who does most of the hunting?

options.label: The resident males
options.rationale: Males sometimes join, but the females lead.

questions.explanation: Lions are carnivores like every cat, and in a pride the females are the primary hunters.
